clause_evidence.reasoning: Every rendered sample (all 18) explicitly asks the learner to compare two measurements and identify which is shorter or longer. No sample requires or tests any behavior beyond comparison. This requirement is fully and consistently exercised across the packet.

Seven samples directly assess length comparison by asking learners to identify which of two object-based measurements is greater or lesser in magnitude. These samples use direct quantities of paperclips, crayons, or hands and isolate the length-comparison task distinct from the spatial-distance variant represented elsewhere in the packet.

Eleven samples directly assess distance comparison by explicitly stating measurements between two locations and asking learners to compare them. Contexts vary (bench to tree, gate to tree) and units include blocks and hands, demonstrating full coverage of the distance dimension.

All 18 samples use non-standard measurement units: paperclips (5 samples), blocks (6 samples), hands (6 samples), and crayons (1 sample). No sample uses metric or standard units. The variety and consistent application of non-standard units throughout the packet demonstrates complete and robust coverage of this requirement.
